extracted.intended_audience: EPA rulewriters, regulators, and stakeholders preparing comments on the 2011 NESHAP proposal for oil & natural gas
extracted.subtask_description: Detailed technical and legal comments on EPA's proposed NESHAP/MACT revisions for Oil and Natural Gas Production and Natural Gas Transmission and Storage, focusing on data, MACT floor setting, LDAR requirements, control technologies, and compliance procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use current and representative data for MACT determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA must recompute the MACT floor and MACT limits using currently available data concerning the performance of the sources within the categories; the 1997/1999/2005 data sets are not representative and EPA's reliance on them is unlawful or flawed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on the 1997/1999 surveys or the 2005 NEI when more recent data (e.g., 2008 NEI or current source data) are available; EPA should collect recent data from the source categories and use the most comprehensive and accurate available data to set floors and limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify best-performing units from actual performance data
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA should determine the 'best performing' sources based on sources that consistently have the lowest leak detection levels, the fewest leaks, and the smallest percentage of 'unrepairable leaks', rather than assigning assumed efficiencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review compliance reports filed by industry over the years to identify best performers; MACT floors must reflect emission levels achieved by relevant best performing units.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate analysis for new-source MACT floors for subcategories
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA should conduct separate examinations of appropriate new source MACT floors and MACT limits for small glycol dehydrators and for storage tanks (including tanks with flash potential and newly regulated tank categories).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small units and new categories require unit-specific analysis rather than lumping into older, non-representative datasets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not ignore technologies that reduce but do not eliminate HAPs
rubrics_metrics.description: Technologies that merely reduce emissions (but do not eliminate them entirely) are valid for consideration in the MACT review and cannot be lawfully dismissed simply because they do not achieve zero HAP emissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For example, desiccant dehydrators and other Natural Gas STAR practices that demonstrably reduce emissions should be evaluated for MACT applicability and potential to strengthen standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibit importing cost-based exemptions into MACT floor determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: Exemptions and deferred repair options that are artifacts of NSPS cost-based reasoning are inappropriate in MACT floor determinations where cost may not be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA must justify any exemptions, quantify their impact on HAP emissions, and avoid exemptions that prevent MACT floors from reflecting best-performing facilities' practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate whether Subpart VVa 500 ppm LDAR threshold represents MACT
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA proposes the 500 ppm leak detection threshold of Subpart VVa rather than the 10,000 ppm of Subpart VV; this is an improvement, but EPA has not shown that Subpart VVa practices represent the existing or new source MACT floor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct a far more comprehensive evaluation of LDAR practices employed in the sector and performance achieved by best facilities before adopting thresholds as MACT.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include all components in hydrocarbon service in LDAR programs
rubrics_metrics.description: The LDAR program should include all components that are in hydrocarbon service; exemptions for components that contact streams with <5% HAP or <10% are inappropriate for MACT determinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such percentage-based exemptions are often cost-based and should not be applied, especially for new sources where jurisdictions (e.g., BAAQMD) require more stringent monitoring without such exemptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condition monitoring deferrals on replacement with leakless technology
rubrics_metrics.description: Monitoring deferrals for equipment designated unsafe/difficult to monitor or requiring shutdown for repair should be conditioned on replacement of deferred equipment with leakless technology at the next facility turnaround.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deferral periods should not exceed five years and should be tied to an obligation to upgrade equipment; do not allow indefinite deferrals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disallow deferred repairs for gross emitters
rubrics_metrics.description: Gross emitters (above a specified emission rate) should not be allowed to continue to emit until the next facility turnaround and should not be eligible for deferred repair times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish emission-rate thresholds limiting the continued use of leaking components and restrict deferrals to components leaking below specified limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require advanced 'zero emissions' or leakless designs for new sources where feasible
rubrics_metrics.description: New sources within the category should be required to employ advanced 'zero emissions technologies' or leakless designs where technically feasible, at a minimum as demonstrated by the best performing source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New-source MACT for LDAR should be no less stringent than leading local rules (e.g., BAAQMD) covering large refineries and should not exempt new compressors at the wellhead from best seal technology requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replace components that repeatedly leak
rubrics_metrics.description: The MACT standard should require a component to be replaced with upgraded technology if the number of leaks within a specified period exceeds a threshold specified in the rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite local rules (SCAQMD, Ventura County APCD) that require replacement when a valve has had >5 major leaks in a year; listing acceptable upgraded control options is advisable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow optical scanning and ultrasound as supplemental LDAR tools, not replacements
rubrics_metrics.description: Optical scanning and ultrasound devices can reduce inspection frequencies and help identify gross emitters but have not been shown to be as effective as LDAR programs and cannot quantify emissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use optical/ultrasound for targeted, frequent scans (daily/weekly) to identify problem areas for LDAR; they can fill gaps and reduce costs without replacing LDAR entirely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calibrate leak monitors using methane and include methane tracking
rubrics_metrics.description: Method 21 monitors should be calibrated using methane and leak thresholds should include the entire organic stream; programs that require methane tracking (e.g., BAAQMD) demonstrate feasibility and should be considered MACT for VOC control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calibrating with methane enhances detection of VHAP in largely methane streams and improves LDAR effectiveness at lower detection limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent auditing of LDAR programs for oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: Given historical widespread LDAR fraud and underreporting, EPA should require detailed, independent oversight such as independent audits of LDAR programs for large sources (perhaps once every five years).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Smaller sources could be exempt if they participate in an industry-sponsored random audit program where a percentage of smaller sources are occasionally audited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recompute MACT floors where prior methods assigned efficiencies
rubrics_metrics.description: For source categories (e.g., storage tanks) where EPA in 1999 assigned an efficiency because data were 'inadequate', EPA must now recompute MACT floors using substantially more complete data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on assigned efficiencies; use representative, contemporary performance data to determine actual emission levels achieved by best-performing units.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set storage tank controls more stringent than 95% when supported
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA's proposal to apply a 95-percent emissions reduction MACT standard to every storage vessel lacks justification; EPA should increase required HAP reduction to 98% or 99% unless it provides a technical explanation based on evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA must discuss analysis and rejection of higher control levels; a move from 95% to 98% represents a 60% reduction in mass emitted and is non-trivial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eliminate alternative compliance options that undermine MACT outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA's proposal to eliminate the benzene <0.9 Mg/yr alternative compliance option for large glycol dehydrators is appropriate; alternatives that allow higher residual risk should be removed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure residual risk analyses are robust; do not assume 'acceptable levels of risk' without addressing flaws and omissions in the risk assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: EPA must conduct thorough 8-year MACT review and consider achievable advances
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA's eight-year section 112(d) MACT review must be thorough; EPA should not conclude no revisions are needed when evidence indicates available technologies, processes, and practices can achieve greater emission reductions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and incorporate advances achieved in industry and by states, and account for enforcement-driven improvements and best practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not normalize emissions data inappropriately
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA's attempt to 'normalize' emissions data (as it did in prior rulemakings) is unlawful and should be abandoned; data manipulation cannot substitute for robust current datasets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use raw representative performance data of sources to set MACT floors and beyond-the-floor analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: MACT floors must reflect maximum achievable reductions (statutory mandate)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA must determine lawful floors reflecting emission levels achieved by relevant best performing units and set MACT standards that reflect the maximum achievable degree of reduction of HAP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both existing- and new-source floors should be based on performance actually achieved, per 42 U.S.C. § 7412(d)(2)-(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not permit permanent leak-rate allowances that frustrate MACT
rubrics_metrics.description: Options that accept a permanent 2 percent leak rate (with allowance to exclude an additional 1 percent 'unrepairable' leaks after the first quarter) are inconsistent with MACT and must be re-evaluated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA should not allow sources to choose the least effective requirement among applicable rules; MACT should require compliance with the most stringent applicable LDAR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit 'nonrepairable' exemptions for new sources to leakless design failures
rubrics_metrics.description: For new sources, EPA should limit the 'nonrepairable' exemption to failures of leakless design components and not broadly allow nonrepairable exemptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prevents gaming of exemptions and ensures new sources deploy the best available designs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish emission-rate thresholds to force repairs or replacements
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA should establish an emission rate threshold that limits the continued use of leaking components and require replacement or more stringent controls when thresholds are exceeded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowable repair deferral limits should be limited to components that leak below the specified limit; gross emitters should be excluded from deferrals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review and incorporate state/local BACT/BAAQMD/SCAQMD rules and consent-decree lessons
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA failed to examine leading state-designed and implemented LDAR programs and enforcement outcomes; it should incorporate lessons learned, including lower detection thresholds, leakless components, and audit requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include BAAQMD rules covering refineries and SCAQMD/Ventura County rules requiring replacement after repeated leaks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use remote scanning to identify problem areas within large component populations
rubrics_metrics.description: Remote optical/ultrasonic scanning should be used to identify plant areas with gross emitters and those not currently monitored, particularly at complexes with tens of thousands of components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remote scans can guide targeted LDAR inspections and reduce scheduled inspections while improving environmental performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider Natural Gas STAR program technologies unless inapplicable
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA should not broadly reject advances from the Natural Gas STAR program as 'new and unproven' where they are not new and are applicable; some STAR technologies are implementable and should be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid painting with too broad a brush; assess each practice/technology for applicability and demonstrated performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require more robust dataset for small dehydrator BTEX limits
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA's proposed unit-specific BTEX limits for small glycol dehydrators are based on outdated data; EPA must base these limits on more robust, current datasets for both production and transmission sectors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure comparability across sectors; resolve counter-intuitive results (e.g., stricter limits for downstream than upstream) by collecting adequate representative emissions data.
